assessment: The importance of vitamin D and its metabolism to maternal and fetal outcomes is well recognized. Both mother and fetus (in terms of skeletal development and birth weight) are heavily dependent on sufficient 25(OH) vitamin D and its conversion to 1,25(OH)2 vitamin D. This interesting work concentrates on the central role of placental function and not maternal physiology to the uptake of 25(OH) vitamin D and its transformation to 1,25(OH)2 vitamin D in determining the availability of vitamin D metabolites to the fetus in pregnancy. This work extends substantially our understanding of fundamental human fetal developmental processes.
